chunks: What Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who buys a camel for sacrifice, then it goes missing before he marks it or garlands it, and he cannot find it until he comes and slaughters [a replacement], and then finds his sacrificial animal.
He عليه السلام said: If he had not marked it, then it remains part of his property: if he wishes, he may slaughter it, and if he wishes, he may sell it. But if he had marked it, he must slaughter it.

key_terms.نَحَرَهَا: he slaughtered it in the prescribed manner for camels
key_terms.يُشْعِرَهَا: to mark the sacrificial animal by ritual incision/sign
key_terms.يُقَلِّدَهَا: to garland the animal as a sign of sacrificial designation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a lost hady animal is found after buying a replacement?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling concerning a sacrificial camel that was lost and then later found after a replacement had been obtained. If the original animal had not yet been formally marked for sacrifice, it remains the owner’s property; but if it had been marked, it must be slaughtered as hady.
